newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-Poor prices to hit SAfrica platinum mines.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Poor prices to hit SAfrica platinum mines.

text.p: Poor precious metal prices could impact on the earnings of South African platinum producers due to report half-year results over the next two weeks -- and the market's further fall paints a grim picture for 1997.
Analysts polled by Reuters varied widely with their profit predictions for the six months to end-December 1996.

"It will be pretty poor. PGM (platinum group metals) prices in dollar terms are substantially less than the previous six months which has partially offset the benefit from the depreciation of the rand," Irish and Menell Rosenburg Inc analyst George Topping told Reuters.
"The annual wage hikes, effective from June, will consume the remainder," he added.
Analysts said the world's biggest platinum producer, Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd, was likely to report flat to higher interim earnings on February 3.
Those forecasting a flat number attributed it to a damaging strike last July.
South Africa's other major producer, Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd (Implats), could lift profits, when it reports on February 11, after a dismal performance last year.

"I think you are going to see two stark contrasts in results. For Impala they are going to be up, last year was a bit of a disaster. Amplats will probably be fairly flat if not downish on the back of the prices," platinum analyst Ross Gardiner of stockbrokers Frankel Pollack said.
Analysts polled by Reuters varied widely on Amplats' earnings forecasts. They said earnings were likely to range from 60 to 125 cents a share from 71.4 cents previously.
They predicted an interim dividend of around 50 cents against the previous 55 cents.

Implats was seen reporting earnings per share of between 110 cents and 155 cents against 149 cents in the corresponding period last year and said the company could declare an interim divided of between 25 and 34 cents.

The analysts said Amplats' results would reflect losses sustained during a mid-year strike in 1996 at its Rustenburg Platinum Mines Holdings Ltd (Rusplats) -- which the company said cost it about 100,000 ounces of platinum in lost production.

"The depreciating rand would have helped them, it offsets the weak platinum rate. But they had quite a substantial strike during July which will set them back a little, platinum produced should be down because of that," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
"Rustenburg is going to be hit severely by the strike but it is going to be taken on the chin, I think," another analyst said.
But some analysts said that overall Amplats's earnings could be boosted by diamond operations and retained profits.
Amplats produces 36 percent of the world's newly-mined platinum.

Although analysts saw Implats performing better, they said Impala would have to account for the hammering it took in forward cover when the company fixed $193 million of anticipated year receipts at 3.92 rand to the dollar.
Since February last year the rand lost 29 percent of its value against the dollar. It was last bid at 4.56 on the dollar.
"Implats have had quite a good six months. The thing that is going to hurt them is the forward cover on the rand they took out," Topping said.

Another analyst said the impact of Implats' forward losses would be cushioned somewhat by the company holding a major supply contract with Ford Motor Co. which saw a six-month lag in the received dollar price of platinum.
